report: A 74-year-old man with prior squamous cell carcinomas had a 6-month tender, enlarging scalp lesion and a 5-mm pink dome-shaped papule, suggesting malignant skin neoplasm. Histology showed SMA-positive perivascular ovoid cells, CD31-positive endothelial channels, mitoses, necrosis, and atypia; melanoma and smooth-muscle markers were negative. Pathologist analysis supports malignant glomus tumor, excluding melanoma, angiosarcoma, and benign lesions. Ki-67 is missing, precluding grading.
